newsitem.title: INDIA: India to make 50 and 100-seater aircraft.
newsitem.headline: India to make 50 and 100-seater aircraft.

text.p: Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Tuesday that India would manufacture 50 and 100-seater aircraft, and welcomed foreign investors to participate in the venture.

"I am happy to announce two major projects..The budget for the project would be made available next financial year," Deve Gowda said, inaugurating a five-day international air-show on the outskirts of the southern Indian city of Bangalore.
He said the aircraft would be produced at the Bangalore based, state-owned Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and the federal government would sanction $230 million for the project.
A top HAL official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters that the aircraft would be mainly used for commercial purposes, but could also be used for military transport.
Gowda welcomed foreign collaborations in the venture and said: "We can cooperate in a manner beneficial to both sides".
"To our friends from other countries, I would like to say that there are ample opportunities for cooperation in the growing Indian economy and in the aviation sector," he added.
International aircraft makers have showed interest in the venture.
"We will follow the developments here and see whether there is a possibility of collaboration," Denis Verret, executive vice-president of Aerospatiale, told Reuters.
"We surely would be interested but it is too early to say anything," said M.J. Thackeray, regional vice-president, sales and marketing of Mcdonnel Douglas.
